bookTitle: Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives (John C. Hull)
generalAssumptions: Interest rate futures trade on standardized short-term interest rates (Eurodollar/SOFR).
Daily mark-to-market settlement induces a positive covariance wedge between futures and forward rates.
Duration and convexity provide first-order and second-order price sensitivities to parallel yield curve shifts.

facts.topic: Eurodollar and SOFR Futures Specifications and Tick Valuation
facts.statement: 3-month Eurodollar futures and 3-month SOFR futures trade on $1,000,000 principal. Prices are quoted on an index basis as 100 minus the annualized interest rate R (Price = 100 - R). The contract tick value for a 1 basis point (0.01%) move is exactly $25 ($1,000,000 * 0.0001 * 90/360 = $25).

variables.definition: Cash value per 0.01% interest rate movement

facts.topic: Futures vs Forward Rates: The Convexity Adjustment
facts.statement: Due to daily mark-to-market settlement, interest rate futures generate cash flows positively correlated with interest rates. This makes futures rates systematically higher than forward rates. The relationship requires a downward convexity adjustment: Forward Rate = Futures Rate - 0.5 * sigma^2 * T1 * T2.

variables.definition: Rate implied by interest rate futures price
Annual volatility of the underlying short rate

facts.topic: Macaulay Duration: Weighted Average Cash Flow Timing
facts.statement: Macaulay duration measures the effective maturity of a bond as the weighted average time until all discounted cash flows are received: D = sum(t_i * C_i * e^(-y * t_i)) / B, where B is the bond market price.

variables.definition: Time until payment of cash flow i
Current clean cash price of the bond

facts.topic: Modified Duration and Linear Price Sensitivity
facts.statement: Modified duration D* provides the direct first-order linear approximation of bond price change per unit shift in yield: Delta B / B approx -D* * Delta y, where D* = D / (1 + y/m).

To immunize a bond portfolio of market value P and duration D_P against parallel yield curve shifts, the optimal number of futures contracts to short is: N* = (P * D_P) / (V_F * D_F), where V_F is the futures contract value and D_F is the duration of the CTD bond.

variables.definition: Optimal number of futures contracts to hedge
Market value of asset bond portfolio
Modified duration of asset bond portfolio
Modified duration of CTD bond at futures maturity

facts.statement: Convexity C accounts for the curvature of the bond price-yield curve: Delta B / B approx -D* * Delta y + 0.5 * C * (Delta y)^2. Because (Delta y)^2 is always positive, positive convexity ensures that bond prices rise faster when yields drop than they fall when yields rise.

facts.topic: Snapshot 6.3: Bank Asset-Liability Management (ALM) Duration Gap
facts.statement: A commercial bank with $1,000M in long-term assets (duration 7.0 years) funded by $900M in deposits (duration 1.0 year) has an unhedged duration gap. A +200 bps yield hike inflicts a -$140M loss on assets while liabilities only gain $18M, producing a net -$122M equity loss that completely wipes out the bank's $100M capital.

numericalDetails.context: Bank insolvency triggered by +200 bps rate shock with 7-year asset duration vs 1-year deposit duration

facts.topic: Corporate Bond Portfolio Duration Hedge Worked Example
facts.statement: A fund manager holds a $50M bond portfolio with modified duration 6.8 years. Treasury futures trade at $98,000 with CTD duration 8.2 years. Total portfolio dollar duration is $340,000,000; single contract dollar duration is $803,600. Sizing the hedge yields N* = 340,000,000 / 803,600 = 423.1 contracts. Shorting 423 contracts immunizes the portfolio against parallel yield spikes.

numericalDetails.context: Optimal short futures contract sizing to immunize a $50M corporate bond portfolio
